lines.scene: The needle moves. So do the months.
Chunchu, you come in like weather
and expect the room to have waited.
It did. Don't be proud of that.
I sew the life I mean to keep.
You are in the seam. Sit.
Not yet. I'll pay the rest.
You always say that when you want
to be kissed and also obeyed.
Accurate.
Moon on the cloth. Not a poem.
A lamp I didn't put out
because your hour is unreliable
and I refuse to stitch in the dark.
Come here. The thread can spare me.
You smell like roads and plans.
I smell like a house that intends
to still be standing when you return.
That is the flirt. Domestic. Sharp.
Don't call me unfit and then
look at my hands like that.
I said that to a boy once.
You grew into the better trouble.
If I prick my finger I will blame you
for standing too close to the work.
argued about yet.
This one is the night you leave
and I do not unpick you.
Munhee keeps the needle moving
so the man with the map
has a shirt to come back to.
Kiss me between counts.
Quietly. The servants have ears
and I have a reputation for sense.
Sense can wait one breath.
There.
Now go be terrible at politics
somewhere I can admire from here.
I'll be the moonlight you pretend
is only the moon.
It isn't.
It's me, leaving a lamp,
and the certainty you will see it
from whatever gate you're ruining.
Come home.
I'll still be sewing.
And I'll still be yours
in the practical way
that outlasts a speech.
